newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS DOWNHILL IN FRENCH FIRST.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND WINS DOWNHILL IN FRENCH FIRST.

text.p: Luc Alphand won a World Cup Alpine skiing downhill on Friday, becoming the first Frenchman to triumph in the Val Gardena classic.

Alphand, the World Cup downhill champion for the past two seasons, clocked an unofficial one minute 53.10 seconds to take victory ahead of Norwegian veteran Atle Skaardal and Italian local favourite Kristian Ghedina in third place.

The downhill replaced one postponed from Whistler Mountain in Canada earlier in the month and was the second of the season. For once the dominant Austrians were pushed not only off the podium but completely out of the top six finishers.
The start was delayed by one hour because of bad weather and the course was shortened with the racers setting off from an altitude of 2,170 metres instead of 2,249.
